title: Give bee-verifying the two-consent split and the commands.test composition rule
verify: bee dev regen && bee dev release-manifest --check
action: Teach bee-verifying how the generated drive command reaches the project's declared test command, and make the user's consent two moments instead of one (per D2 and D7). Add a section to skills/bee-verifying/SKILL.md covering five things. (1) TWO MOMENTS. Moment one builds the skill and proves it by running it once: cheap, reversible, touches no configuration. Moment two comes AFTER that proof run and asks a separate question carrying the MEASURED wall-clock the run actually took, because that number is what the user is really agreeing to. Never bundle the two into one yes; a user who wanted proof their app works has not thereby agreed to permanently slower commits. On a no at moment two, the skill stays and stays manual, and that answer is recorded so the question is not asked again unprompted. (2) THE COMPOSITION. Append, never replace: an existing declared command becomes `<existing> && <drive>`; a project with none gets the drive alone. If the declared command is a JSON array rather than a string, append one element rather than string-concatenating. Appending twice is a defect - check for the drive already being present before writing. (3) THE bash PREFIX. The drive is always invoked as `bash <path> ...`, never as a bare path, because bee's renderer does not carry the executable bit into a rendered copy - a bare path fails with Permission denied on the first onboard of every host. State the reason in one line so a later reader does not 'fix' it back. (4) WHERE TO WRITE IT. `bee config set` is not built - it refuses with `command_unavailable` and its own FIX line says to read and edit .bee/config.json directly, so that is the sanctioned path here and the skill says so, naming the refusal as the reason. (5) THE FAST/FULL SPLIT. The generated skill must expose a fast scoped drive for the per-change loop and a full sweep for CI, and it is the FAST one that composes into the declared command; state that as the contract the generated control script has to satisfy. Do not touch any Rust file, and do not add a door, gate or proof tier. Finish with the regen chain so all five committed trees carry the new body.
